parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of the series. Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: Form the ratio of consecutive terms.
Take the limit as n goes to infinity.
The series converges when the limit is less than 1.
At x = 5 the series is the harmonic series, a p-series with p = 1, which diverges.
At x = -1 the series is the alternating harmonic series; its terms decrease to 0, so it converges by the alternating series test.

points.criterion: Writes the ratio of consecutive terms, the (n+1)th term over the nth term, which simplifies to n|x - 2| / (3(n + 1)), with or without absolute values.

Evaluates the limit of the ratio as n tends to infinity correctly as |x - 2|/3, written with correct limit notation (lim with n tending to infinity) and with absolute value or a squared inequality that is then resolved. A simplification or evaluation error in the limit, or an equality between the n-dependent ratio and the limit with no lim written, does not earn it.
Resolves the inequality to the interior -1 < x < 5, as a two-sided inequality or an open interval. When an incorrect but positive limit was found, the matching interior earns it.
Substitutes both endpoints, x = -1 and x = 5, and writes the two resulting numerical series.

Analyses both endpoint series correctly with an appropriate test named or clearly identified (x = 5: harmonic or p-series with p = 1, or the integral test, diverges; x = -1: alternating series test, converges) and states the interval -1 <= x < 5. An interval with no endpoint analysis, or endpoint analysis that follows from a reciprocal ratio, does not earn it.
